beats.caption: Take-or-pay: buy the minimum volume or pay for it anyway
beats.text: A take-or-pay or long-term supply agreement commits a buyer to purchase a set minimum over several years. If the buyer takes less, it still owes the money. In AI, buyers sign these to lock in scarce memory, GPUs or compute.

beats.caption: Prepayments give the seller cash to build capacity
beats.text: Some deals come with money up front. Memory makers have taken customer prepayments to help fund new fabs, and the commitment lets them add capacity knowing it is already sold.

beats.caption: Supply flows to the buyer at the committed rate
beats.text: While demand is strong, the buyer gets guaranteed supply when others are rationed. Cloud providers sign multi-year compute commitments with neoclouds on the same logic: capacity reserved, price fixed.

beats.caption: When demand falls, the buyer still pays
beats.text: If the buyer needs less, the product piles up or the reserved capacity sits idle, but the minimum payment keeps flowing. The seller is protected; the risk sits with the buyer.

beats.caption: Find them under purchase obligations in filings
beats.text: Filings list these as purchase commitments or contractual obligations, often billions over several years. Rising obligations show confidence or a scramble for supply. Related: Micron (MU), NVIDIA (NVDA), CoreWeave (CRWV), Microsoft (MSFT), Western Digital (WDC).
